chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muawiya ibn 'Ammar, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who performed Hajj and did not touch the Stone, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'It is from the Sunnah. So if he is not able, then Allah is closer to excusing (him).'

key_terms.أَوْلَى بِالْعُذْرِ: closer to the excuse / more deserving of considering the excuse
key_terms.يَسْتَلِمِ الْحَجَرَ: to touch the Stone (specifically the Black Stone)

ai.seo_question: Is touching the Black Stone mandatory for Hajj to be valid?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the legal status of Istilam (touching/kissing the Black Stone) as a confirmed Sunnah rather than a fard (obligatory) pillar, emphasizing divine mercy in cases of inability due to crowding. This ruling underscores the Shia principle that ritual acts retain their spiritual merit even if physical performance is hindered, provided the intention remains sincere. The Imam’s statement 'Allah is more worthy of excuse' highlights the theological concept of God's comprehensive knowledge of the pilgrim's constraints, relieving them of sin for omission.
